objective: Select the best national party-strength forecast from historically available pre-election information before any 2026-specific signal can affect the numeric national forecast.
principle: The national layer is an empirical forecasting problem, not a political-evidence aggregation exercise.

optional_fold.gate: USE_ONLY_IF_A_COMPLETE_AND_COMPARABLE_NATIONAL_PARTY_SHARE_VECTOR_CAN_BE_CERTIFIED; partial 2002 district vote matrices must not be silently completed

candidate_family_policy.small_sample_guardrail: Prefer a small preregistered family with shrinkage; do not search an unrestricted model space over three principal folds.
candidate_family_policy.entrant_exit_policy: Party births, mergers, disappearances and OTHER must use an explicit historically reproducible crosswalk; no retroactive knowledge of target outcomes.

selection.primary_metric: equal-weight mean fold compositional party-share RMSE
selection.winner_rule: Choose the preregistered candidate with the lowest primary metric unless it fails a predeclared stability or entrant/exit integrity gate.

incremental_input_admission.rule: A new pre-election information class may affect the 2026 national forecast only if the same class can be reconstructed comparably before historical target elections and adding it improves rolling-origin national forecast skill out of sample under a frozen transformation.

national_uncertainty_gate.method: Calibrate national forecast residuals from strict rolling-origin errors of the selected national model, using shrinkage/variance floors appropriate to the small number of independent election transitions.
